findings.description: A completion turn can append an open question and then crash or return invalid JSON. Both failure exits (review.go:660 and review.go:665) bypass the conversation read at review.go:685, leaving only the original empty findings in the coverage park. Consequently axi --yes and TUI yolo see no review-question category and automatically approve without an answer. Re-read and append conversation findings after every attempted completion turn, including both failure paths, before returning the parked outcome.

The completion merge drops completion.WithdrawnFindings. During an answer-finalize round, the first turn can omit feature2.txt and leave its carried finding unadjudicated; the focused turn then reads it and explicitly retracts that finding using the supplied answers. Only items, coverage, and risk are merged here, so review.go:538 returns the first turn's retractions instead. The executor keeps the disproved finding outstanding because answer-round silence cannot clear it. Merge the completion's named retractions too, preserving id and reason. This must hold for ordinary finalize rounds and finalize rounds with Fixing/SkipFixExecution, which share review.go:520 and review.go:654.

The new EvalReplay bypass benchmarks a different review protocol from the captured production round. For a two-file case, production can report no findings on file one, discover a defect during coverage completion on file two, and capture that defect as selected gold. Replaying the same candidate with the same first response now skips the discovering turn, recording a false negative and artificially lower cost. The claim that capture does not charge completion also contradicts capture.go:438. Remove this replay-only mode unless benchmarking the truncated protocol is explicitly intended. Related sites: pipeline.go:39 (flag), review.go:629 (bypass), review_coverage_retry_test.go:640 (pins bypass), pipeline-steps.md:98 and SKILL.md:116 (claim equivalent replay).

Concrete sequence: get_active_run observes review running, so preAnswer is nil (axi_answer.go:125); review parks before the answer arrives; the answer resumes it; finalize parks again before getRunInfo completes. findings.description: The post-answer fallback can adopt the finalize turn's new gate as the gate being released. Concrete sequence: get_active_run sees review running, the question gate registers before the answer arrives, the answer resumes it, and the finalize turn parks before getRunInfo returns. The fallback captures that new round and waits for it to leave, withholding the decision until --wait expires. This affects both awaiting_approval and fix_review, including the older-daemon Resumed path. Related sites: internal/cli/axi_answer.go:125 captures only already-parked gates; internal/cli/axi_answer.go:242 waits on the guessed identity; internal/cli/axi_drive.go:1073 cannot distinguish a new gate once its own identity was adopted. Only perform the initial wait with an identity captured before answering; otherwise use the existing drive/question-grace loop, which already handles late stale question parks.

The completion merge drops completion.WithdrawnFindings. On an answer-finalize round, the first turn can cover feature.txt and leave a carried feature2.txt finding unadjudicated; the focused turn then covers feature2.txt and explicitly withdraws that finding with a reason. findings.description: The post-answer gate-inference fallback can mistake the next gate for the released gate. Concrete sequence: get_active_run observes review still running, leaving preAnswer nil (lines 121-125); review parks before the answer arrives; the answer resumes it; finalize parks again before getRunInfo returns. Both awaiting_approval and fix_review, and the Resumed compatibility path at line 226, are affected. This inference is unnecessary: the bounded question-park loop at lines 246-266 already handles parks not observed before answering. Remove the fallback rather than inferring a released gate from post-answer state. Removing this deliberate matching path is the remedy requiring approval.

Both early returns (review.go:660 and review.go:665) bypass the conversation read at review.go:685, leaving only the original clean, partial findings. The resulting coverage-only gate has no review-question category, so axi --yes and TUI yolo automatically approve it despite the unanswered question. Re-read the conversation after every attempted coverage turn, before either failure return, using the shared helper at review.go:738.

The completion merge drops withdrawn_findings. During an answer round, the first turn can omit a carried finding on an uncovered file; the completion turn receives the answers and carried findings through review.go:655, examines that file, and explicitly withdraws the finding. Only Items and ReviewedPaths are merged (review.go:676-677), so the outcome at review.go:541 forwards no such withdrawal. The executor consequently retains the disproved finding and parks again. Merge the completion's explicit retractions into the round's withdrawal list.

The EvalReplay bypass benchmarks a different review pass from the captured source. For example, production initially omits feature2.txt, then its completion discovers a defect that becomes captured gold; replaying the same reviewer stops after the initial omission and records a false negative without charging the completion. This is not merely unused certification: completion contributes source findings. Related sites are pipeline.go:39 (mode), eval/replay.go:314 (activation), and eval/capture.go:438 (baseline includes completion cost), contradicting the stated uncharged-baseline rationale. Please authorize this distinct one-turn benchmark explicitly or remove the bypass to replay the complete review pass.

The blanket empty-findings guard discards valid source-risk assessments, not just deferred-delivery risk. A first turn can report low risk while omitting a fundamental migration file; completion can cover that file, find no specific defect, and legitimately report medium/high source risk under the prompt's risk rules. The merged output silently remains low/clean. The same policy is asserted in docs/src/content/docs/reference/pipeline-steps.md:97 and .agents/skills/pipeline-review-and-agents/SKILL.md:117. Please confirm this deliberate restriction; otherwise preserve the worse source assessment and limit suppression to risk actually attributable to stripped delivery findings.
